note: The main banks read are Banco Basa (kept from before) and Itaú Paraguay, the largest card issuer whose terms could be read; Banco Continental's site sits behind Cloudflare, ueno's refused the request behind Cloudflare and Banco GNB's behind Akamai. Banco Basa's tariff report for October 2026, read in full: its seven personal cards (Cabal, Mastercard or Visa Clásica, Mastercard Farmacenter Clásica, Mastercard or Visa Oro Basa, Mastercard Farmacenter Oro, Visa Signature and Mastercard Black), each with the main card's yearly fee; loans by credit card bear a nominal 18.05% a year (19.62% effective); a cash advance, local or abroad, costs 9.90% of it, at least 25,000 guaraníes; purchases abroad cost 2.2% on the Clásica and Oro cards and nothing on the Signature, Black and Oro Basa (the tariff lists 'Basa' among the exempt). Itaú Paraguay's rates and charges in force (conditions for October 2026), read in full: its seventeen personal cards, each with the main card's yearly fee (none on the Clásica ex Touring, 24 HS IN / Práctica American Express, Visa Básica and Centenario cards, whose holder's fee is a dash); normal financing bears a nominal 18.04% a year (19.61% effective), the same at the table's minimum and maximum; a cash advance costs 8.25% of it, at least 26,400 guaraníes on the bank's network; the conversion factor the card brands add to purchases abroad, 1% on Visa and Mastercard and 2% on American Express, is written as the foreign transaction fee. Its E-CARD (82,500 a year) isn't said to be a credit card and isn't written; nor are its business cards. At both banks the interest is subject to VAT, at a rate neither tariff states, so it isn't added; the punitive interest (up to 30% of the compensatory rate, on top of it) isn't written as a penalty rate. No minimum payment, grace period or late fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Interfisa Banco, the next card-issuing bank whose own tariff a plain request reached: its rates and tariffs in force for October 2026 (published under the Banco Central del Paraguay's resolutions), read in full: credit card loans bear a nominal 10.00% to 17.92% a year (10.52% to 19.62% effective), written at the top with the bottom as the range's lowest; the sheet says interest bears VAT at 10%, written as the tax on interest; each personal card's yearly fee for the main card (the Visa and Mastercard Clásica 200,000 guaraníes, Gold 330,000, Visa Platinum 925,000, Mastercard Black and Visa Signature 1,100,000), with a monthly maintenance of 16,500 and 2.20% on purchases abroad on the Clásica cards (the other cards show a dash in both columns, written as no charge stated); a minimum payment of 5% of the capital; a cash advance of 8.80%, at least 21,000. The Gourmet Card isn't a credit card and isn't written; the moratory interest (at most the agreed rate) and the punitive interest (up to 30% of the moratory rate) aren't written, as for the other banks; the 55,000 recovery charge on a card in arrears is a collection charge per event and isn't written. No grace period is stated. Tried and not used: Banco Sudameris's site sits behind Incapsula and the Banco Central del Paraguay's behind a Cloudflare check; Banco Familiar's card pages link no tariff; Visión Banco's, Banco Atlas's and Banco Río's didn't answer.
